title.zh: 卷六十二 志第三十一: 刑法下
title.raw: 卷六十二 志第三十一: 刑法下 Volume 62 Treatises 32: Punishment and Law 2

sentences.zh: 刑法志下

translations.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Punishment and Law, Part Two

sentences.zh: 興宗即位，欽哀皇后始得志，昆弟專權。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xingzong took the throne, Empress Dowager Qin'ai at last had her way, and her brothers monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzong came to the throne, Empress Dowager Qin'ai finally had her way, and her brothers seized control of the government.

sentences.zh: 馮家奴等希欽哀意，誣蕭浞卜等謀反，連及嫡後仁德皇后。

translations.literal: Feng Jianu and others, courting Qin'ai's favor, falsely accused Xiao Hubu and others of plotting rebellion, implicating the legitimate empress Ren'ade.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jianu and others, eager to please Qin'ai, framed Xiao Hubu and his associates for treason and dragged in the legitimate empress, Ren'ade.

sentences.zh: 浞卜等十餘人與仁德姻援，坐罪者四十餘輩皆被大辟，仍籍其家。

translations.literal: More than ten men including Hubu were related to Ren'ade by marriage; over forty persons convicted in the case were all sentenced to death, and their households were registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Hubu and more than ten others were connected to Ren'ade by marriage; over forty people implicated in the case were executed, and their families' property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 幽仁德於上京，既而遣人弒之。

translations.literal: Ren'ade was confined at Shangjing, and afterward men were sent to assassinate her.
translations.idiomatic: Ren'ade was imprisoned at Shangjing, and assassins were soon sent to kill her.

sentences.zh: 迫殞非命，中外切憤。

translations.literal: Forced to die before her time, court and country alike were deeply outraged.
translations.idiomatic: Her violent death stirred fierce indignation throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 欽哀後謀廢立，遷於慶州。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Qin'ai plotted deposition and enthronement, and was transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin'ai plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone another, she was banished to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及奉迎以歸，頗復預事，其酷虐不得逞矣。

translations.literal: When she was escorted back in welcome, she again took part in affairs to a considerable degree, yet her cruelty could no longer be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: When she was brought back to court, she again meddled in state affairs, but she could no longer carry out her cruelties at will.

sentences.zh: 然興宗好名，喜變更，又溺浮屠法，務行小惠，數降赦宥，釋死囚甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet Xingzong loved reputation, delighted in change, and was also infatuated with Buddhist law, striving to dispense small favors; he repeatedly issued amnesties and released a great many condemned prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xingzong cared deeply for his reputation, loved to change policy, and was devoted to Buddhism; he showered petty favors, issued frequent amnesties, and released a great many prisoners under sentence of death.

sentences.zh: 重熙元年，詔職事官公罪聽贖，私罪各從本法；

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, an edict stated that functional officials' public offenses might be redeemed, while private offenses were each punished according to the applicable statute;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongxi, an edict allowed functional officials to redeem public offenses, while private offenses were punished under the usual statutes;

sentences.zh: 子弟及家人受賕，不知情者，止坐犯人。

translations.literal: when sons, younger brothers, and household members accepted bribes, those who did not know were punished only as to the offender himself.
translations.idiomatic: when sons, younger brothers, or household members took bribes, those who did not know were not punished—only the guilty party was.

sentences.zh: 先是，南京三司銷錢作器皿三斤，持錢出南京十貫，及盜遺火家物五貫者處死；

translations.literal: Previously, at the Nanjing Three Departments, melting coin to make vessels of three jin, carrying ten strings of cash out of Nanjing, and stealing or leaving fire-damaged household goods worth five strings were punished by death;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, melting three jin of coin into vessels at the Nanjing Three Departments, carrying ten strings of cash out of Nanjing, or stealing—or through fire, destroying—household goods worth five strings were capital crimes;

sentences.zh: 至是，銅逾三斤，持錢及所盜物二十貫以上處死。

translations.literal: at this time, copper exceeding three jin, and carrying cash or stolen goods of twenty strings or more, were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: now death applied only when copper exceeded three jin, or when cash carried or goods stolen amounted to twenty strings or more.

sentences.zh: 二年，有司奏：「元年詔曰，犯重罪徒終身者，加以捶楚，而又黥面。

translations.literal: In the second year, the responsible offices memorialized: "The edict of the first year states that those guilty of serious crimes and sentenced to lifetime penal servitude are to receive beating in addition, and also facial tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the responsible offices reported: "The first-year edict provides that offenders guilty of serious crimes and sentenced to lifetime penal servitude are beaten and also tattooed on the face.

sentences.zh: 是犯一罪而具三刑，宜免黥。

translations.literal: This is one offense bearing three punishments; facial tattooing should be waived."
translations.idiomatic: One offense thus carries three punishments; facial tattooing should be waived."

sentences.zh: 其職事官及宰相、節度使世選之家子孫，犯奸罪至徒者，未審黥否？

translations.literal: As for functional officials and the descendants of hereditary-selection families of chancellors and military commissioners, when guilty of adultery punishable by penal servitude, it is not yet clear whether they are to be tattooed?"
translations.idiomatic: For functional officials and descendants of hereditary chancellor and military commissioner families, when adultery is punished by penal servitude, should facial tattooing still apply?

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「犯罪而悔過自新者，亦有可用之人，一黥其面，終身為辱，朕甚憫焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor instructed: "Those who offend yet repent and renew themselves may still be of use; once the face is tattooed, it is a lifelong disgrace — We are deeply moved to pity."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Some who commit crimes and truly repent may still be useful; a single mark on the face is a lifelong disgrace, and We pity them deeply."

sentences.zh: 」後犯終身徒者，止刺頸。

translations.literal: " Thereafter, those guilty of lifetime penal servitude were tattooed only on the neck.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter, lifetime penal servitude was marked by tattoo on the neck alone.

sentences.zh: 奴婢犯逃，若盜其主物，主無得擅黥其面，刺臂及頸者聽。

translations.literal: When male and female slaves committed flight or theft of their master's goods, the master might not on his own authority tattoo their faces; tattooing the arm or neck was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When slaves fled or stole their master's property, masters might not tattoo their faces on their own authority; tattooing the arm or neck was permitted.

sentences.zh: 犯竊盜者，初刺右臂，再刺左，三刺頸之後，四刺左，至於五則處死。

translations.literal: Petty thieves were first tattooed on the right arm, a second time on the left, after a third on the neck a fourth on the left; upon the fifth offense they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Petty thieves were first marked on the right arm, then the left, then the neck, then the left again; on the fifth offense they were executed.

sentences.zh: 五年，《新定條制》成，詔有司凡朝日執之，仍頒行諸道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the "Newly Fixed Regulations" were completed; the emperor ordered the responsible offices to apply them on every court day and also to promulgate them through all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the "Newly Fixed Regulations" were completed; officials were ordered to apply them at every court session and to promulgate them throughout all circuits.

sentences.zh: 蓋纂修太祖以來法令，參以古制。

translations.literal: They compiled and revised statutes from Taizu onward, with reference to ancient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: They compiled statutes from Taizu onward and drew on ancient models.

sentences.zh: 其刑有死、流、杖及三等之徒而五，凡五百四十七條。

translations.literal: Its punishments were death, exile, beating, and five grades of penal servitude in three terms, five hundred forty-seven articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: The code defined death, exile, beating, and five grades of penal servitude in three terms—five hundred forty-seven articles in all.

sentences.zh: 時有群牧人竊易官印以馬與人者，法當死，帝曰：「一馬殺二人，不亦甚乎？

translations.literal: At the time there were herd-masters who secretly exchanged official seals to trade horses to others; by law they should die. The emperor said: "To kill two men for one horse — is that not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: Some herd-masters had secretly swapped official seals to trade government horses; the statute called for death. The emperor said, "To execute two men over one horse—is that not excessive?"

sentences.zh: 」減死論。

translations.literal: " Their sentence was reduced from death.
translations.idiomatic: " The sentence was commuted from death.

sentences.zh: 又有兄弟犯強盜當死，以弟從兄，且俱無子，特原其弟。

translations.literal: There were also brothers guilty of armed robbery who should die; because the younger followed the elder and both were without sons, the younger was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers guilty of armed robbery faced execution; because the younger had followed the elder and neither had sons, the younger was specially spared.

sentences.zh: 至於枉法受賕，詐敕走遞，偽學御書，盜外國貢物者，例皆免死。

translations.literal: As for perverting the law to accept bribes, forging edicts to flee by relay post, counterfeiting imperial calligraphy, and stealing tribute goods from foreign states — by precedent all were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Those who perverted the law for bribes, forged edicts to flee by relay post, counterfeited imperial calligraphy, or stole foreign tribute were routinely spared execution.

sentences.zh: 郡王貼不家奴彌裏吉告其主言涉怨望，鞫之無驗，當反坐，以欽哀皇后裏言，竟不加罪，亦不斷付其主，僅籍沒焉。

translations.literal: The household slave Miliji of Prince Junwang Tiebu reported his master for words suggesting resentment; interrogation found no proof, and by law the accuser should be punished in turn; because of Empress Dowager Qin'ai's private word, he was in the end not punished, nor adjudged and returned to his master — only his property was registered for confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: Miliji, a slave of Prince Junwang Tiebu, accused his master of disloyal speech; the charge could not be proved and the accuser should have been punished in turn, but at Qin'ai's private word he escaped punishment, was not returned to his master, and only had his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 寧遠軍節度使蕭白強掠烏古敵烈都詳穩敵魯之女為妻，亦以後言免死，杖而奪其官。

translations.literal: Xiao Bai, military commissioner of Ningyuan Army, forcibly seized the daughter of Dile, detailed commander of the Uighur and Tatar tribes, as wife; he too was spared death on the empress's word, beaten, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bai, commissioner of Ningyuan Army, forcibly took Dile's daughter as his wife; he too was spared death on the empress's word, beaten, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 梅裏狗丹使酒殺人而逃，會永壽節出首，特赦其罪。

translations.literal: Meilidoudan, drunk, killed a man and fled; it happened to be the Eternal Longevity festival, and he surrendered himself; his crime was specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Meilidoudan killed a man in a drunken rage and fled; he surrendered on the Eternal Longevity festival and received a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 皇妹秦國公主生日，帝幸其第，伶人張隋，本宋所遣汋者，大臣覺之以聞。

translations.literal: On the birthday of the emperor's sister, Princess of Qin, the emperor visited her residence; the actor Zhang Sui, originally a spy sent by Song, was detected by a great minister who reported it.
translations.idiomatic: On his sister the Princess of Qin's birthday the emperor visited her residence; the actor Zhang Sui, originally a Song spy, was detected and reported by a senior minister.

sentences.zh: 召詰，款伏，乃遽釋之。

translations.literal: Summoned and questioned, he confessed fully, yet was forthwith released.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned and questioned, he confessed fully—and was immediately released.

sentences.zh: 後詔諸職官私取官物者，以正盜論。

translations.literal: Later an edict stated that functional officials who privately took government goods were to be judged as full theft.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ruled that officials who privately took government property were guilty of full theft.

sentences.zh: 諸帳郎君等於禁地射鹿，決杖三百，不徵償；

translations.literal: Various account gentlemen who shot deer in forbidden ground were sentenced to three hundred strokes, without compensation levied;
translations.idiomatic: Account gentlemen who shot deer in the imperial preserve were sentenced to three hundred strokes, without compensation;

sentences.zh: 小將軍決二百已下；

translations.literal: junior generals received two hundred strokes or less;
translations.idiomatic: junior generals received two hundred strokes or fewer;

sentences.zh: 至百姓犯者決三百。

translations.literal: commoners who offended received three hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: commoners who offended received three hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 聖宗之風替矣。

translations.literal: The style of Emperor Shengzong had declined.
translations.idiomatic: The standards of Shengzong's reign were gone.

sentences.zh: 道宗清寧元年，詔諸宮都部署曰：「凡有機密事，即可面奏；

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingning, Emperor Daozong edicted the palace chief deployments: "Whenever there are confidential matters, you may memorialize in person;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingning, Daozong ordered the palace chief deployments: "Report confidential matters to Us in person;

sentences.zh: 餘所訴事，以法施行，有投誹訕之書，其受及讀者皆棄市。

translations.literal: all other suits are to be carried out according to law. Whoever submits writings of slander — both the receiver and the reader are to be executed in the marketplace."
translations.idiomatic: all other suits shall follow the law. Anyone who receives or reads a slanderous writing shall be executed in the marketplace."

sentences.zh: 」二年，命諸郡長吏如諸部例，與僚屬同決罪囚，無致枉死獄中。

translations.literal: " In the second year, he ordered prefectural chief administrators, following the tribal precedent, to decide criminal cases together with their subordinates, so that none should die wrongfully in prison.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year he ordered prefectural administrators, following tribal precedent, to decide criminal cases jointly with their staffs so that no one would die wrongfully in prison.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「先時諸路死刑皆待決於朝，故獄訟留滯；

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Formerly capital sentences in all circuits awaited decision at court, so litigation was delayed;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Formerly all capital sentences in the circuits awaited court decision, and litigation piled up;

sentences.zh: 自今凡強盜得實者，聽即決之。

translations.literal: from now on, wherever armed robbery is proved, let judgment be immediate."
translations.idiomatic: from now on, wherever armed robbery is proved, the local office may execute judgment at once."

sentences.zh: 」四年，復詔左夷離畢曰：「比詔外路死刑，聽所在官司即決。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year, he again edicted the Left Yilipin: "The recent edict allowed capital punishment on outer circuits to be decided on the spot by the local office.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth year he again instructed the Left Yilipin: "The recent edict allowed local offices on the outer circuits to decide capital cases on the spot.

sentences.zh: 然恐未能悉其情，或有枉者。

translations.literal: Yet We fear the circumstances may not be fully known, and some may be wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet We fear the facts may not be fully known and innocents wronged.

sentences.zh: 自今雖已款伏，仍令附近官司覆問，無冤然後決之，有冤者即具以聞。

translations.literal: From now on, even when confession is complete, nearby offices are still to re-examine; only when there is no injustice shall sentence be carried out; where injustice exists, report in full."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, even after full confession, nearby offices must re-examine the case; only when no injustice is found may sentence be carried out; any sign of wrongful conviction must be reported."

sentences.zh: 」咸雍元年，詔獄囚無家者，給以糧。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Xianyong, an edict provided grain to prisoners without families.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Xianyong, prisoners without families were supplied with grain.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝以契丹、漢人風俗不同，國法不可異施，於是命惕隱蘇、樞密使乙辛等更定《條制》。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the emperor held that Khitan and Han customs differed and state law could not be applied differently; he therefore ordered Tiyin Su, Privy Councilor Yixin, and others to revise the "Regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor held that Khitan and Han customs differed and national law could not be applied in two ways; he ordered Tiyin Su, Privy Councilor Yixin, and others to revise the "Regulations."

sentences.zh: 凡合於《律令》者，具載之；

translations.literal: Whatever accorded with the "Statutes and Ordinances" was fully recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever accorded with the "Statutes and Ordinances" was fully recorded;

sentences.zh: 其不合者，別存之。

translations.literal: what did not accord was kept separately.
translations.idiomatic: what did not accord was kept in a separate register.

sentences.zh: 時校定官即重熙舊制，更竊盜贓二十五貫處死一條，增至五十貫處死；

translations.literal: The revising officers, taking the Chongxi old system, changed the article on theft punishing twenty-five strings of booty with death to fifty strings for death;
translations.idiomatic: The revisers, working from the Chongxi code, raised the death penalty for theft from twenty-five to fifty strings of booty;

sentences.zh: 又刪其重復者二條，為五百四十五條；

translations.literal: deleted two duplicate articles, making five hundred forty-five;
translations.idiomatic: deleted two duplicate articles, leaving five hundred forty-five;

sentences.zh: 取《律》一百七十三條，又創增七十一條，凡七百八十九條，增重編者至千餘條。

translations.literal: took one hundred seventy-three articles from the "Statutes," and newly added seventy-one, seven hundred eighty-nine in all; with additions and heavy revisions the total reached more than a thousand articles.
translations.idiomatic: they took one hundred seventy-three articles from the "Statutes" and added seventy-one new ones—seven hundred eighty-nine in all; with further additions and revisions the total exceeded a thousand.

sentences.zh: 皆分類列。

translations.literal: All were arranged by category.
translations.idiomatic: All were arranged by category.

sentences.zh: 以大康間所定，復以《律》及《條例》參校，續增三十六條。

translations.literal: Based on what had been fixed in the Dakang period, they again collated against the "Statutes" and "Regulations," adding thirty-six articles.
translations.idiomatic: Building on the Dakang code, they collated it again against the "Statutes" and "Regulations" and added thirty-six articles.

sentences.zh: 其後因事續校，至大安三年止，又增六十七條。

translations.literal: Thereafter they continued revision as cases arose; by the third year of Da'an they stopped, having added sixty-seven more articles.
translations.idiomatic: Revision continued case by case until the third year of Da'an, when sixty-seven more articles were added.

sentences.zh: 條約既繁，典者不能遍習，愚民莫知所避，犯法者眾，吏得因緣為奸。

translations.literal: Once the regulations grew numerous, custodians of the law could not master them all; simple people did not know what to avoid; offenders were many, and clerks used the occasion to practice deceit.
translations.idiomatic: As the code grew bloated, officials could not master it, common people did not know what to avoid, offenses multiplied, and clerks exploited the confusion for private gain.

sentences.zh: 故五年詔曰：「法者所以示民信而致國治，簡易如天地，不忒如四時，使民可避而不可犯。

translations.literal: Therefore in the fifth year an edict stated: "Law is that by which the people's trust is shown and the state brought to order — simple as Heaven and Earth, unerring as the four seasons, so that the people may avoid offense yet not dare to violate it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in the fifth year an edict declared: "Law exists to win the people's trust and bring order to the state—it should be as plain as Heaven and Earth, as steady as the four seasons, so that people may know what to avoid and dare not transgress.

sentences.zh: 此命有司纂修刑法，然不能明體朕意，多作條目，以罔民於罪，朕甚不取。

translations.literal: We ordered the responsible offices to compile and revise penal law, yet they could not make clear Our intent, and made many articles to entangle the people in guilt — We greatly disapprove.
translations.idiomatic: We ordered the offices to revise the penal code, yet they failed to grasp Our intent and multiplied articles to trap the people in crime—We will not accept this.

sentences.zh: 自今復用舊法，余悉除之。

translations.literal: From now on the old law is again to be used; all the rest is abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the old law alone shall apply; all additions are abolished."

sentences.zh: 」然自大康元年，北院樞密使耶律乙辛等用事，宮婢單登等誣告宣懿皇后，乙辛以聞，即詔乙辛劾狀，因實其事。

translations.literal: " Yet from the first year of Dakang, Northern Privy Councilor Yelü Yixin and his faction held power; palace maid Shan Deng and others falsely accused Empress Xuanyi; Yixin reported it, and an edict at once ordered Yixin to investigate the charge — thereby making the accusation fact.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet from the first year of Dakang, Northern Privy Councilor Yelü Yixin held power; palace maid Shan Deng falsely accused Empress Xuanyi; Yixin reported it, and the emperor ordered him to investigate—thereby making the charge stick.

sentences.zh: 上怒，族伶人趙惟一，斬高長命，皆籍其家，仍賜皇后自盡。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; the actor Zhao Weiyi was punished with extinction of kin; Gao Changming was beheaded; both households were registered for confiscation; the empress was still ordered to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage: the actor Zhao Weiyi and his entire clan were destroyed, Gao Changming was beheaded, both families' property was confiscated, and the empress was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 三年，乙辛又與其黨謀構昭懷太子，陰令右護衛太保耶律查剌，告知樞密院事蕭速撒等八人謀立皇太子。

translations.literal: In the third year, Yixin again plotted with his faction to frame Crown Prince Zhaohuai, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to report that Privy Councilor Xiao Susa and eight others plotted to enthrone the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yixin and his faction framed Crown Prince Zhaohuai, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse Privy Councilor Xiao Susa and eight others of plotting to enthrone the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 詔按無狀，出速撒、達不也外補，流護衛撒撥等六人。

translations.literal: An edict investigated and found no substance; Susa and Dabuye were sent out for external appointment; six guards including Sapo were exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation found no substance; Susa and Dabuye were posted elsewhere; six guards including Sapo were exiled.

sentences.zh: 詔告首謀逆者，重加官賞；

translations.literal: An edict stated that whoever reported the chief plotters of rebellion would receive heavy promotion and reward;
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised heavy promotion and reward to whoever reported the chief plotters of treason;

sentences.zh: 否則悉行誅戮。

translations.literal: otherwise all would be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise all involved would be executed.

sentences.zh: 乙辛教牌印郎君蕭訛都斡自首「臣嘗預速撒等謀」，因籍姓名以告。

translations.literal: Yixin coached Seal Office Gentleman Xiao Eduo to surrender himself, saying "Your servant once took part in Susa's plot," and thereby registered names to inform against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yixin coached Seal Office Gentleman Xiao Eduo to confess: "I once took part in Susa's plot," and Eduo denounced others by name.

sentences.zh: 帝信之，以乙辛等鞫按，至杖皇太子，囚之宮中別室，殺撻不也、撒剌等三十五人，又殺速撒等諸子；

translations.literal: The emperor believed it; Yixin and others conducted the inquiry, going so far as to beat the crown prince and imprison him in a separate chamber within the palace; Tabuye, Sala, and thirty-five others were killed, and Susa's sons were also killed;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed them; Yixin conducted the inquiry, had the crown prince beaten and imprisoned in a separate palace chamber, executed Tabuye, Sala, and thirty-five others, and killed Susa's sons as well;

sentences.zh: 其幼稚及婦女、奴婢、家產，皆籍沒之，或分賜群臣。

translations.literal: their infants, women, male and female slaves, and household property were all registered for confiscation, or distributed as gifts among the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: their children, wives, slaves, and property were confiscated or distributed among the ministers.

sentences.zh: 燕哥等詐為太子爰書以聞，上大怒，廢太子，徙上京，乙辛尋遣人弒於囚所。

translations.literal: Yange and others forged the crown prince's written pledge and reported it; the emperor was greatly enraged, deposed the crown prince, and transferred him to Shangjing; Yixin soon sent men to assassinate him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yange and others forged the crown prince's confession; the emperor deposed him and sent him to Shangjing, where Yixin soon had him murdered in prison.

sentences.zh: 帝猶不寤，朝廷上下，無復紀律。

translations.literal: The emperor still did not awaken; above and below the court, discipline was no more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still did not see the truth, and discipline vanished from the court.

sentences.zh: 天祚乾統元年，凡大康三年預乙辛所害者悉復官爵，籍沒者出之，流放者還鄉里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiantong under Tianzuo, all who in the third year of Dakang had suffered at Yixin's hands had rank and titles restored; those whose property had been registered were released; those exiled returned to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianzuo's first year of Qiantong, all whom Yixin had harmed in the third year of Dakang had rank and titles restored, confiscated property returned, and exiles sent home.

sentences.zh: 至二年，始廢乙辛等墓，剖棺戮屍，誅其子孫，餘黨子孫減死，徙邊，其家屬奴婢皆分賜被害之家。

translations.literal: By the second year, Yixin's tomb and others were at last destroyed, coffins opened and corpses flogged, his descendants executed; descendants of the remaining faction had death reduced and were moved to the border; their household members and slaves were all distributed as gifts to the families of the victims.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yixin's tomb was destroyed, his coffin opened and corpse flogged, his descendants executed; other faction members' descendants had sentences reduced and were exiled, their families and slaves given to the victims' kin.

sentences.zh: 如耶律撻不也、蕭達魯古等，黨人之尤凶狡者，皆以賂免。

translations.literal: Such men as Yelü Tabuye and Xiao Dalugu — the most vicious and cunning of the faction — all escaped through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yelü Tabuye and Xiao Dalugu, the faction's most vicious members, all bought their way free.

sentences.zh: 至於覆軍失城者，第免官而已。

translations.literal: As for those who lost armies or cities, they were merely dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Generals who lost armies or cities were merely dismissed.

sentences.zh: 行軍將軍耶律涅裏三人有禁地射鹿之罪，皆棄市。

translations.literal: Campaign General Yelü Nieli and three others were guilty of shooting deer in forbidden ground; all were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign General Yelü Nieli and three others who shot deer in the imperial preserve were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 其職官諸局人有過者，鐫降決斷之外，悉從軍。

translations.literal: Functional officials and bureau personnel who offended, beyond inscription, demotion, and judgment, were all sent to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and bureau staff who offended, beyond demotion and formal judgment, were all sent to the army.

sentences.zh: 賞罰無章，怨讟日起；

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments lacked rule; resentment and complaint arose daily;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments had no rhyme or reason; resentment mounted daily;

sentences.zh: 劇盜相挺，叛亡接踵。

translations.literal: fierce bandits rose one after another, and defection and flight followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: banditry spread and defections followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 天祚大恐，益務繩以嚴酷，由是投崖、炮擲、釘割、臠殺之刑復興焉。

translations.literal: Tianzuo was greatly afraid and strove all the more to bind men with severity; thereby casting from cliffs, cannon-throwing, nailing and cutting, and dismemberment killings revived.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo, terrified, tightened the law with ever greater cruelty; casting from cliffs, cannon-throwing, nailing, cutting, and dismemberment were revived.

sentences.zh: 或有分戶五京，甚者至取其心以獻祖廟。

translations.literal: Some had their households divided among the Five Capitals; in extreme cases hearts were taken to offer at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Some offenders' families were split among the Five Capitals; in the worst cases their hearts were taken as offerings at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 雖由天祚救患無策，流為殘忍，亦由祖宗有以啟之也。

translations.literal: Although Tianzuo, having no strategy to save the realm from disaster, drifted into cruelty, the ancestors too had given him cause to begin it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tianzuo, lacking any strategy to save the realm, drifted into cruelty, his ancestors had shown him the way.

sentences.zh: 遼之先代，用法尚嚴。

translations.literal: Liao's early generations still valued severity in applying law.
translations.idiomatic: The early Liao rulers applied the law with notable severity.

sentences.zh: 使其子孫皆有君人之量，知所自擇，猶非祖宗貽謀之道；

translations.literal: Even if their descendants all possessed the measure of rulers and knew how to choose for themselves, this would still not be the way ancestors bequeath counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Even if every descendant possessed true kingly stature and knew how to choose wisely, severity alone is not how ancestors bequeath good counsel;

sentences.zh: 不幸一有昏暴者，少引以藉口，何所不至。

translations.literal: if by misfortune there should be one benighted and violent, he need only cite it slightly as pretext — what limit would there be?
translations.idiomatic: but let one benighted tyrant cite that precedent, and there is no limit to what he may do.

sentences.zh: 然遼之季世，與其先代用刑同，而興亡異者何歟？

translations.literal: Yet Liao's final age applied punishment like its forebears — why were rise and fall different?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the late Liao applied punishment much as the early dynasty had—why did one flourish and the other perish?

sentences.zh: 蓋創業之君，施之於法未定之前，民猶未敢測也；

translations.literal: The founding ruler applied it before the law was fixed; the people still did not dare to fathom him;
translations.idiomatic: The founding ruler enforced severity before the law was fully codified, and the people still could not predict his will;

sentences.zh: 亡國之主，施之於法既定之後，民復何所賴焉。

translations.literal: the ruler who lost the state applied it after the law was already fixed — upon what could the people again rely?
translations.idiomatic: the last ruler enforced it after the law was fixed, and the people had nothing left to rely on.

sentences.zh: 此其所為異也。

translations.literal: This is wherein their conduct differed.
translations.idiomatic: That is the difference.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「新國輕典。

translations.literal: The Classic of Documents says: "A new state uses light statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "A new state uses light statutes."

sentences.zh: 」豈獨權事宜而已乎？

translations.literal: " Was this merely weighing expedients for the occasion?
translations.idiomatic: " Was that merely a matter of expedience?

sentences.zh: 天祚未年，遊畋無度，頗有倦勤意。

translations.literal: In Tianzuo's last years he hunted without measure and showed considerable weariness of governing.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years Tianzuo hunted without restraint and showed signs of weariness with rule.

sentences.zh: 諸子惟文妃所生敖盧斡最賢。

translations.literal: Among his sons, only Aoluwo, born of Consort Wen, was most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Of all his sons, only Aoluwo, born of Consort Wen, was truly worthy.

sentences.zh: 蕭奉先乃元妃兄，深忌之。

translations.literal: Xiao Fengxian was the elder brother of the Primary Consort and deeply envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fengxian, elder brother of the Primary Consort, deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 會文妃之女兄適耶律撻曷裏，女弟適耶律余睹，奉先乃誣告余睹等謀立晉王，尊天祚為太上皇。

translations.literal: It happened that Consort Wen's elder daughter by marriage was wed to Yelü Tahieli and her younger to Yelü Yudu; Fengxian then falsely reported that Yudu and others plotted to enthrone the Prince of Jin and honor Tianzuo as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wen's elder daughter was married to Yelü Tahieli and her younger to Yelü Yudu; Fengxian then falsely accused Yudu and others of plotting to enthrone the Prince of Jin and make Tianzuo Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 遂戮撻曷裏及其妻，賜文妃自盡。

translations.literal: Tahieli and his wife were thereupon executed; Consort Wen was ordered to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: Tahieli and his wife were executed, and Consort Wen was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 敖盧斡以不與謀得免。

translations.literal: Aoluwo escaped because he had not joined the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Aoluwo was spared because he had not joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 及天祚西狩奉聖州，又以耶律撒八等欲劫立敖盧斡，遂誅撒八，盡其黨與。

translations.literal: When Tianzuo went west on campaign to Fengshengzhou, it was again reported that Yelü Saba and others wished to seize him and enthrone Aoluwo; Saba was executed and his entire faction destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianzuo marched west to Fengshengzhou, he was told that Yelü Saba and others meant to seize him and enthrone Aoluwo; Saba was executed and his entire faction destroyed.

sentences.zh: 敖盧斡以有人望，即日賜死。

translations.literal: Because Aoluwo enjoyed popular esteem, that same day he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Because Aoluwo enjoyed popular esteem, he was ordered to die that same day.

sentences.zh: 當時從行百官、諸局承應人及軍士聞者，皆流涕。

translations.literal: All the officials on the march, bureau attendants, and soldiers who heard it wept.
translations.idiomatic: Every official, bureau attendant, and soldier on the march who heard of it wept.

sentences.zh: 蓋自興宗時，遽起大獄，仁德皇后戕於幽所，遼政始衰。

translations.literal: From the time of Xingzong, great prisons were suddenly raised; Empress Ren'ade perished in confinement — Liao government began to decline.
translations.idiomatic: From Xingzong's reign great purges began; Empress Ren'ade died in confinement—and Liao governance began its decline.

sentences.zh: 道宗殺宣懿皇后，遷昭懷太子，太子尋被害。

translations.literal: Daozong killed Empress Xuanyi, transferred Crown Prince Zhaohuai, and the crown prince was soon murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong killed Empress Xuanyi and banished Crown Prince Zhaohuai, who was soon murdered.

sentences.zh: 天祚知其父之冤，而己亦幾殆，至是又自殺其子敖盧斡。

translations.literal: Tianzuo knew his father's wrongful death, and he himself had nearly perished; at this point he again killed his own son Aoluwo.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo knew the injustice done to his father and had himself nearly died for it; now he killed his own son Aoluwo.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「於所厚者薄，無所不薄矣。

translations.literal: The "Commentary" says: "Where one is sparing toward those he favors, he will be sparing toward all."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says, "He who is sparing toward those he favors will be sparing toward everyone."

sentences.zh: 」遼二百餘年，骨肉屢相殘滅。

translations.literal: " For more than two hundred years Liao, flesh and bone repeatedly destroyed one another.
translations.idiomatic: " For more than two hundred years the Liao royal house repeatedly destroyed its own kin.

sentences.zh: 天祚荒暴尤甚，遂至於亡，噫！

translations.literal: Tianzuo was especially benighted and violent, and thus came to ruin — alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo was more benighted and violent than any before him, and so the dynasty fell — alas!
